newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish one-year bond min price seen down at tender.
newsitem.headline: Polish one-year bond min price seen down at tender.

text.p: The minimum price of Polish one-year index-linked bonds is expected to fall at Tuesday's 348 million zloty primary tender with demand not exceeding 100 million, analysts said on Monday.
They said that investors would likely bid for lower prices on Tuesday after recent increases in the maximum yield of the 52-week T-bill to 20.40 percent at the last primary tender.

"The minimum price will fall because there are currently better investment opportunities on the market...such as T-bills, two- and five-year bonds, CPs and CDs," said Piotr Korcz from Bank Handlowy SA.

Dealers said the minimum price of the one-year bond, whose coupon is the cumulated inflation rate of 12 months ending in December 1997, may fall to around 92.5 against 93.5 at the last auction on January 28, 1997.
They said foreign investors were not interested in Polish one-year bonds as the floater's yield was more difficult to forecast and the paper was not liquid.
At the last auction of the bonds on January 28, the treasury cut the minimum price of the bonds to 93.50 from 96.67. The average price was also down to 94.10 from 96.74.
The value date for this auction is on February 3, 1997.
The next auction of these bonds is sheduled on February 25, 1997.
